newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady, crude sinks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady, crude sinks.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Friday in thin trade, but the complex remained hampered by sagging East Coast utility demand and further weakness in crude, industry sources said.
"This is a shoulder month. There's been no demand, but relative to gas, fuel is pretty low," said one East Coast utility, adding the utility planned to burn fuel this month.

New York Harbor physical one percent held steady at $14.25 a barrel, with May one percent paper also little changed in the $14.15-40 area. Traders said June paper, which sold Thursday at $14.85, eased slightly with crude to $14.60-85.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour remained pegged at $15.25.
High sulphurs in New York also were stable, with 2.2 percent still talked around $14, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent slipped 15 cents to $14.25-50 on talk a seller was offering three cargoes of Colombian material for May delivery.
USG three percent held steady at $13.25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate weekend gas prices were unchanged Friday in the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed a couple of cents to about $2.20/mmBtu, or $13.86 a barrel.
